To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the occurrence of NB and MN in MSCs can affect their proliferative potential and genetic stability.

(i) MSCs from different sources show difference in the frequency of NB and MN; (ii) the occurrence of NB and MN is directly proportional to senescence of the MSCs; (iii) MSCs with high NB and MN show longer G2‐M phase and S phase; (iv) the occurrence of high NB and MN is inversely proportional to their rate of proliferation; (v) the frequency of NB/MN is increased in MSCs on cryopreservation;
the number of nuclear blebs (NB) and micronuclei (MN) in human mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), isolated from the same patient, depends on the source of cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of nuclear blebs (NB) and micronuclei (MN) in human umbilical cord mesenchymal (UC‐MSC) and placental mesenchymal cells (PD‐MSC).
the study of the influence of nuclear blebs and micronuclei status on the growth kinetics of mesenchymmal stem cells (MSC).
the influence of nuclear blebs (NB) and micronuclei (MN) in human mesenchymal stromal cells (hMSCs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of NBs and micronuclei is not only a sign of genetic instability but also a sign of senescence in the cells, and the presence of these structures is associated with a decrease in cell proliferation and an increase in cell senescence.
the presence of NBs and/or MNs in MSC is a marker of senescent cells, which may be due to the activation of DNA damage response pathways.

the occurrence of NB and MN in MSCs is an indicator of the genetic instability of the cells and the presence of these structures in MSCs should not be ignored as a quality control check for MSCs before using these cells for cellular therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of NBs and micronuclei in MSCs is an indication of their genetic instability, which can affect their proliferation rate and differentiation potential.

the frequency of NB and MN is a reliable marker for the genetic stability and quality of MSCs and hence it should be used to assess the quality of these cells before using them for clinical applications.

the presence of nuclear blebs and micronuclei in mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), which are used in regenerative medicine and cellular therapy, is associated with their senescence and genetic instability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the occurrence of nuclear blebs and micronuclei in MSCs is a reflection of their genetic instability and hence their potential to cause tumour formation.
the presence of micronuclei and nuclear blebs is a quality control measure that should be checked before using MSCs for cellular therapy as it is associated with the genetic stability of the cells.
the number of nuclear blebs (NB) and micronuclei (MN) can be used as a quality control marker for the genetic stability of mesenchymall stem cells (MSC).
